shortDescription: Crafts tipped arrows from a normal potion (lingering potions still work too).
oneLiner: Tipped arrows can be crafted with an ordinary potion in the middle of eight arrows, so you no longer need Dragon's Breath and a brewing detour just to tip a stack.

optionalMods.whatItAdds: With JEI installed, TippedArrowsJeiPlugin shows the widened recipe in the recipe browser - one display-only entry per registered potion, centre slot showing the normal and the lingering potion. Without JEI nothing is lost functionally: the recipe still works at a crafting table, it is simply invisible in any recipe browser (and, being a CustomRecipe that overrides neither getResultItem nor isSpecial, it cannot be surfaced by the vanilla recipe book either). JEI is compileOnly plus localRuntime, is declared in no dependency block of neoforge.mods.toml (which lists only neoforge, create, toughasnails, sable, bluemap, minecraft), and the @JeiPlugin class is only ever loaded by JEI's own annotation scan - no ModList.isLoaded gate is needed or present.
optionalMods.evidence: src/main/java/net/geraldhofbauer/vanillaplusadditions/modules/tipped_arrows/compat/jei/TippedArrowsJeiPlugin.java:36 (@JeiPlugin), :48-81 (registerRecipes, module gate at :49-51, addRecipes at :80); build.gradle:110-111 (compileOnly jei-*-common-api / jei-*-neoforge-api), :113 (localRuntime jei-*-neoforge); src/main/resources/META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml:62-115 (no jei dependency)

events: net.neoforged.neoforge.event.AddReloadListenerEvent (TippedArrowsModule.onAddReloadListener, @SubscribeEvent; the module instance registers itself on NeoForge.EVENT_BUS in onInitialize, TippedArrowsModule.java:56, and the handler returns early unless isModuleEnabled(), :66-68. It is the module's only event handler.)
recipes: Replaces vanilla's minecraft:tipped_arrow special recipe in place (same id, via RecipeManager.replaceRecipes): 8 Arrows around a centre potion -> 8 Tipped Arrows carrying the centre potion's POTION_CONTENTS, but the centre slot now accepts a normal minecraft:potion in addition to minecraft:lingering_potion. The centre item's contents are never checked, so water bottles and effectless brews qualify too.

Registers the recipe serializer vanillaplusadditions:potion_tipped_arrow (SimpleCraftingRecipeSerializer for PotionTippedArrowRecipe) - needed so the replaced recipe can be synced to clients; it is not a craftable thing itself.
JEI only, never in the RecipeManager: one display ShapedRecipe per entry of BuiltInRegistries.POTION, id vanillaplusadditions:tipped_arrow_display/<potion path>.
notes:
CORRECTION (2026-09-20, commit 25325d4) - THIS SUPERSEDES ANY STATEMENT BELOW ABOUT PACKAGING.
`tipped_arrows` IS in build.gradle's `standaloneModules` list and builds as `vpa_tipped_arrows` (entrypoint standalone/tipped_arrows/TippedArrowsStandalone.java, needs vpa_core). Its JEI plugin now gates on `TippedArrowsModule.isModuleActive()` instead of a ModuleManager id lookup, which returned false in every standalone jar.
Everything further down that calls the module bundle-only, says it has no standalone jar, or reports a grep over build.gradle returning nothing was written before that commit and is out of date. The rest of the research below is unaffected.

SCOPE (re-verified with find + grep, not taken over from the previous pass): the module is exactly three Java files - modules/tipped_arrows/TippedArrowsModule.java (105 lines), modules/tipped_arrows/recipe/PotionTippedArrowRecipe.java, modules/tipped_arrows/compat/jei/TippedArrowsJeiPlugin.java. No config/ package (the module passes AbstractModuleConfig::createDefault into super(), TippedArrowsModule.java:49, so it gets DefaultModuleConfig, which adds nothing beyond the base enabled + debug_logging - AbstractModuleConfig.java:57-68, :202-208). No mixins (nothing named tipped_arrows in vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json). No standalone entrypoint (no standalone/tipped_arrows/ directory, no 'tipped' anywhere in build.gradle). No lang keys, no assets, no data files: grep -rn 'tipped' over src/main/resources/ returns zero hits, and find over src/main/resources for *tipped*/*arrow* finds nothing. The only reference outside the module directory is VanillaPlusAdditions.java:35 (import) + :192 (registerModule).

HOW IT HOOKS IN: it does NOT add a second recipe. applyTippedArrowRecipe (TippedArrowsModule.java:72-83) builds a RecipeHolder under vanilla's own id ResourceLocation.withDefaultNamespace("tipped_arrow"), copies every existing recipe into a LinkedHashMap, overwrites that one key (LinkedHashMap.put keeps the original insertion position) and calls recipeManager.replaceRecipes(...). Vanilla's TippedArrowRecipe is therefore replaced in place. With the module off the listener is never added at all (isModuleEnabled() guard, :66-68), so vanilla's lingering-only recipe stays untouched - no config migration, no stranded items. The whole recipe map is rebuilt on every datapack reload / server start, not once. This snapshot-and-replace pattern is house style, not a one-off: 13 other modules call recipeManager.replaceRecipes the same way (custom_crafting_recipes, flying_fish, cat_guardian, end_conduit, battle_dogs, stationary_chunk_loader, minecart_chunk_loading, train_chunk_loading, mob_cart_loader, axolotl_guardian, pathfinder_quills, compass_overhaul). Each listener snapshots the map when its own task runs on the game thread, so they compose instead of clobbering each other.

WHY side = "both" (the gameplay part is server-side, but the module's own code really does run on the client): the recipe replacement itself is server-side - AddReloadListenerEvent carries the server resources, and PotionTippedArrowRecipe.matches/assemble run in the server's crafting menu. What makes this module more than 'server' is (a) the DeferredRegister for the recipe serializer is registered on the MOD event bus (TippedArrowsModule.java:55), i.e. on both physical sides, and the client instantiates PotionTippedArrowRecipe itself when the server syncs the replaced minecraft:tipped_arrow recipe; and (b) TippedArrowsJeiPlugin is a client-only display class. Note the contrast with custom_crafting_recipes (fact sheet says "server"): that module injects plain vanilla ShapedRecipe/ShapelessRecipe objects, so no code of its own ever runs client-side. Here it does.

SERIALIZER vs. ENABLED-GATE - the one real risk (unverified in game, do NOT document as confirmed behaviour): the DeferredRegister is only bound to the mod bus inside onInitialize() (:55). ModuleManager.initializeModules (ModuleManager.java:83-110) first filters by ModulesConfig.isModuleEnabled(module) (:92) and then calls initialize() only for that filtered list (:107); AbstractModule.shouldInitialize() is the interface default 'return true' here, i.e. the gate is the config-filtered loop, not the module. Net effect: with tipped_arrows disabled, vanillaplusadditions:potion_tipped_arrow is not in the RECIPE_SERIALIZER registry at all, although the static field itself is created (the module object is always constructed, VanillaPlusAdditions.java:192). A client with the module disabled joining a server with it enabled therefore has no serializer for the synced minecraft:tipped_arrow recipe. Flag as a suspected config-mismatch hazard. NB this is a mod-wide pattern (every module registers its DeferredRegisters in onInitialize), not a tipped_arrows-specific mistake.

RUNTIME TOGGLE (/vpa module enable|disable|clear <id>, VanillaPlusAdditions.java:236-267, :392-409) behaves asymmetrically here and neither direction is instant: DISABLE sets a runtime override that isModuleEnabled() picks up (AbstractModule.java:202-216 -> ModuleManager.resolveModuleEnabled :205-208), but the already-replaced recipe stays live until the next datapack reload, because the guard only runs when the reload listener is (re-)added. ENABLE at runtime can never work at all: onInitialize() ran only for modules enabled at startup, so for a module that started disabled the NeoForge.EVENT_BUS registration (:56) never happened and no AddReloadListenerEvent handler exists. Both directions need a restart (plus, for disable, a reload) to be fully effective.

POTION CONTENTS ARE NEVER INSPECTED (undocumented side effect): isPotionSource (PotionTippedArrowRecipe.java:74-76) only checks stack.is(Items.POTION) || stack.is(Items.LINGERING_POTION) - the item type, never the contents. So a Water Bottle and the effectless Mundane/Thick/Awkward brews are valid centre ingredients too, exactly as they are for vanilla's lingering variant. Concretely a plain (non-lingering) Water Bottle now produces 8 arrows carrying water potion contents - vanilla calls those Arrows of Splashing and normally requires a LINGERING water bottle for them. Caveat for the doc: the 'Arrow of Splashing' naming and the exact contents of a fresh water bottle are vanilla behaviour and are NOT provable from this repository. Edge case from the same lines: assemble (:60) copies whatever get(POTION_CONTENTS) returns; if that is null (a potion-item stack with the component removed) the result ends up with no POTION_CONTENTS, i.e. a plain, effectless tipped arrow rather than a failed craft.

RESULT COMPONENTS: assemble() (PotionTippedArrowRecipe.java:52-62) builds new ItemStack(Items.TIPPED_ARROW, 8) and copies DataComponents.POTION_CONTENTS verbatim, so custom effects, custom potion names and modded potions carry over unchanged. Nothing else is copied (a custom item name on the potion does not travel). getRemainingItems() is not overridden, so the glass bottle behaves exactly as it does for vanilla's recipe (consumed). canCraftInDimensions requires >= 3x3 while matches() requires exactly 3x3 - same asymmetry vanilla's TippedArrowRecipe has.

NOT IN THE VANILLA RECIPE BOOK: PotionTippedArrowRecipe extends CustomRecipe and overrides neither getResultItem nor isSpecial, so it inherits vanilla's special-recipe behaviour (empty result item) and cannot be surfaced by the recipe book. The commit message calls the JEI plugin a way 'to keep the recipe book display working', which is loose wording - JEI is a separate browser, the vanilla recipe book is not involved. (The CustomRecipe superclass is not in this repo, so this rests on vanilla semantics plus the absence of overrides.)

JEI: TippedArrowsJeiPlugin is display-only. It loops over all of BuiltInRegistries.POTION with no filtering beyond a null-key guard and generates one ShapedRecipe per potion (AAA/APA/AAA, centre = Ingredient.of(normal potion, lingering potion), result = 8 tipped arrows with that potion's contents), ids vanillaplusadditions:tipped_arrow_display/<potion path>. They go to JEI via registration.addRecipes(RecipeTypes.CRAFTING, ...) (:80) and never enter the RecipeManager. The plugin re-checks ModuleManager.getInstance().isModuleEnabled("tipped_arrows") itself (:49-51), so a disabled module shows nothing. Side effect for docs: every registered potion gets its own JEI page - including the flavourless mundane/thick/awkward ones and anything other mods add - so the crafting category gets long.

CROSS-MODULE: the stackables module raises the default MAX_STACK_SIZE of Items.POTION/SPLASH_POTION/LINGERING_POTION/TIPPED_ARROW to default_potion_stack_size (default 64, StackablesModule.java:73-81, StackablesConfig defineInRange at :80-82). There is no code link in either direction, but in the bundle with stackables on, both the centre potion and this recipe's 8-arrow output stack to 64. Search trap while researching: modules/stackables/constant_items/StackableTippedArrowItem.java is an unreferenced leftover (grep finds no use anywhere in src/) - it belongs to stackables, not here, and is not the mechanism stackables actually uses.
